atomic.problem:
For the $\alpha$ decay of ${ }^{238} \mathrm{Pu}$, the energy of a single decay is 

$$
E_{\mathrm{d}} = E_{\alpha} + E_{\mathrm{U}} = \frac{p_{\alpha}^2}{2 m_{\alpha}} + \frac{p_{\mathrm{U}}^2}{2 m_{\mathrm{U}}} = E_{\alpha}\left(1 + \frac{m_{\alpha}}{m_{\mathrm{U}}}\right) = \frac{238}{234} \times 5.5 = 5.6(\mathrm{MeV})
$$

Its half-life is $T = 87.75$ years $\approx 2.8 \times 10^9 \mathrm{~s}$, and the decay constant is 

$$
\lambda = \ln 2 / T = 2.5 \times 10^{-10}(\mathrm{~s}^{-1})
$$

The decay energy per unit time for $238 \mathrm{~g}$ of ${ }^{238} \mathrm{Pu}$ is 

$$
\begin{align*}
\frac{\mathrm{d} E}{\mathrm{~d} t} & = E_{\mathrm{d}} \frac{\mathrm{~d} N}{\mathrm{~d} t} = E_{\mathrm{d}} \lambda N_{0} = 5.6 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-10} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \\
& = 8.4 \times 10^{14}(\mathrm{MeV} \cdot \mathrm{~s}^{-1})
\end{align*}
$$

atomic.problem:
When the number of ${ }^{238} \mathrm{Pu}$ nuclei decreases over time, its output power also decreases,

$$
W(t) = W(0) \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda t}
$$

When $W(t_0) = \frac{W(0)}{8}$, this marks the limit time $t_0$ for using ${ }^{238} \mathrm{Pu}$ as a power source for the instrument,

$$
t_0 = \frac{\ln 8}{\lambda} = \frac{3 \ln 2}{\lambda} = 3 T_{1/2} \approx 270 \text { years }
$$

With 238 grams of ${ }^{238} \mathrm{Pu}$ as the energy source, the instrument can operate for 270 years.
